title: Indifferentiability of CMC or EME from an Ideal Tweakable Cipher
summary: CMC and EME have been proved strong pseudorandom permutations, but whether either is indifferentiable from an ideal tweakable cipher remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: The receiver-binding analysis of committing Encode-then-Encipher assumes an ideal variable-input-length tweakable cipher, meaning that a fresh uniformly random permutation is drawn for each distinct key--tweak pair. CMC and EME are mature variable-input-length tweakable-cipher constructions proved to be strong pseudorandom permutations, but it is unknown whether either is indifferentiable from an ideal tweakable cipher. Determine whether CMC or EME, possibly after suitable modification, satisfies this indifferentiability requirement and can therefore instantiate the ideal cipher assumed by the analysis.

scope.domain: Cryptographic design and security analysis of variable-input-length tweakable ciphers for committing authenticated encryption.
assumptions: The receiver-binding analysis assumes an ideal variable-input-length tweakable cipher.
A fresh uniformly random permutation is drawn for each distinct key--tweak pair.
parameters: CMC and EME: candidate mature variable-input-length tweakable-cipher constructions
